(PER : HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE SUNITA AGARWAL) The present petition has been filed on 19.07.2019 with the prayers that the acquisition proceedings with respect to the subject land namely the land bearing Block No. 258, Survey No. 246/2 and Survey No. 240,
total admesuring 42,273 sq.mtrs. situated at village Sachin, Taluka Chorasiya, District Surat shall be declared as NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/12546/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/03/2026 undefined having been lapsed in view of Section 24 of the the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short 'Act, 2013').
The petitioners have also prayed for a mandamus restraining the respondents from taking possession of the subject land pending hearing of the writ petition.

2. Pertinent is to note that on the first date of the presentation of the writ petition, by order dated 23.07.2019, the matter has been adjourned sine die noticing that the issue with regard to the interpretation of Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013 was subject matter of consideration before the Constitution Bench of the Apex Court.

The learned counsel for the petitioners was, however,
directed to file a note on the outcome of the said case.

3. Pertinent is to note that the Constitution Bench of the Apex Court has rendered its decision on 06.03.2020, but no application whatsoever has been filed by the petitioners to place the matter on board.
The petition is listed from the cut off today for the first time, as per the listing methodology adopted by this Court.

4. As regards the interpretation of Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013, the conclusions of the Constitution Bench Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal and others [(2020) 8 SCC 129] are in paragraph No.366.
5.

entities.text: Constitution Bench Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal and others [(2020) 8 SCC 129]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A careful reading of the decision of the Constitution Bench in Indore Development Authority (supra) indicates that the correct interpretation of Section 24 of the Act, 2013 was subject matter of reference to the five-Judge Bench of the Apex Court.

It was held therein that the word 'or' used in Section 24(2) between NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/12546/2019 JUDGMENT DATED:
02/03/2026 undefined the possession and compensation has to be read as 'nor' or as 'and'.

The deemed lapse of the land acquisition proceedings under Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013 takes place where due to inaction of the authorities for five years or more prior to the commencement of the said Act (2013 Act), the possession of the acquired land has not been taken nor compensation has been paid.
In other words, in case possession has been taken, but the compensation has not been paid, then there is no lapse.
Similarly, if the compensation has been paid, possession has not been taken then there is no lapse.

As far as the provisions of Section 24(1)(b) of the Act, 2013, it is held that where award has been passed within the window of five years excluding the period covered by any interim order of the Court, then the proceedings shall continue as provided under the 1894 Act,
as if it has not been repealed.

For a case where the award is not made as on 01.01.2014, i.e. the date of commencement of 2013 Act, as per the provisions of Section 24(1)(a), compensation has to be Amratlal Dharamchand Shah Since Decd. ... vs State Of Gujarat on 2 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41425540/
2 determined under the provisions of the Act, 2013 and there is no lapse of proceedings.

6. It is clarified that the expression 'paid' in the main part of sub-section(2) of Section 24 of the Act,
2013 does not include a deposit of the compensation in Court.

The consequence of non- deposit is provided in the proviso to Section 24(2), in case it has not been deposited with respect to majority of landholdings, then all beneficiaries/land owners as on the date of notification for land acquisition under Section 4 of the Act, 1894 shall be entitled to compensation in accordance with the provisions of the 2013 Act.

At the most, in case the obligation under Section 31 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 has not been fulfilled, interest under Section 34 of the 1894 Act can be granted.
Non-deposit of compensation (in Court) does not result in lapse of land acquisition proceedings.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/12546/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/03/2026 undefined 7.

It is further clarified that, in case, the person has been tendered compensation, as provided under Section 31(1) of the 1894 Act, it is not open to him to claim that acquisition has lapsed under Section 24(2) due to non-payment or non-deposit of the compensation in the Court.
The obligation to pay is complied by tendering the amount under Section 31(1).

The land owners who had refused to accept the compensation or who sought reference for higher compensation, cannot claim that the acquisition proceedings had lapsed under Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013.
8.
It is also clarified that the mode of taking possession under the 1894 Act and as contemplated under Section 24(2) is by drawing of inquest report/memorandum.

Once the award has been passed on taking possession under Section 16 of the 1894 Act, the land vests in the State and there is no divesting provided under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act, hence once the possession has been taken by drawing of panchnama/inquest report/memorandum, there is no lapse under Section 24(2).
9.

The Apex Court has categorically held that the provisions of Section 24(2) providing for a deemed lapse of the proceedings, are applicable in case the authorities have failed due to their inaction to take possession and pay compensation for five years or more before the 2013 Act came into force.

Any proceedings for land acquisition pending with the authorities concerned as on 01.01.2014, the period of subsistence of interim order passed by the Court, if any, has to be excluded for the computation of 5 years.
The further clarification under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act, does not give rise to new cause of action to question the legality of the concluded proceedings of the land acquisition.

Section 24 applies to the proceedings pending on the date of enforcement of the 2013 NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/12546/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/03/2026 undefined Act i.e.
01.01.2014.

It does not revive stale and time barred claims and does not reopen the concluded proceedings nor allow the land owners to question the legality of mode of taking of possession to reopen the proceedings or mode of deposit of compensation in the treasury instead of Court to invalidate the acquisition.

10. Taking note of the above observations of the Constitution Bench while answering the scope of interpretation of Section 24 of the Act, 2013, we are required to revert to the facts of the present case.

The petitioners herein claim to be the owners of the land-in- question and would submit that their names were duly mutated in the revenue records upon death of original owner and the entry of Amratlal Dharamchand Shah Since Decd. ... vs State Of Gujarat on 2 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41425540/

sentences.text: their names was certified on 29.06.1986.
On 11.02.1988, notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was issued.
Section 6 notification in furtherance thereof was published on 01.02.1989.
The notice under Section 9 was published on 15.02.1989 and thereafter, the Special Land Acquisition officer had declared the award on 14.02.1991.
As per the own case of the petitioner, the panchnama was drawn on 5.5.1996 though it is sought to be contended that the possession was taken only on paper.

11. The petitioners then contended that the landholders of the village Sachin had declined to accept the compensation and to handover the possession of all the lands which were sought to be acquired by the aforesaid notifications.

Inspite of the said fact, the mutation entries were made with respect to the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer and the notice dated 27.02.2004 under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was published.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/12546/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/03/2026 undefined 12.

The reference has been made to the various letters issued by the competent authorities to assert that neither the compensation had been received by the landholders nor possession of the subject land had been taken though the paper possession has been taken by drawing of the panchnama.

The contention is that even after expiry of 28 years from the date of making of the award dated 14.02.1991, prior to the commencement of the 2013 Act, neither the physical possession of the land has been taken nor compensation has been paid to the petitioners.
13.

This contention made by the petitioners in the memo of the writ petition specifically indicates that acquisition proceedings came to its logical end with the making of the award in the year 1991 itself.

The notice under Section 12(2) had been issued, as per the own case of the petitioner, on 27.02.2004 by the Collector giving intimation of the award to the persons interested, who were not present personally or by their representatives when the award was made.
It is not the case of the petitioners that the process of disbursement of compensation had not been undertaken after issuance of the notice under Section 12(2) of the Act, 2013.

Even otherwise, with the drawing of panchnama on 05.05.1996, as per the own case of the petitioners, after making of the award on 14.02.1991, there is no question of applicability of Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013.

14. As clarified by the Apex Court in Indore Development Authority (supra) the provisions of Section 24(2) providing for deemed lapse of the proceedings are applicable only in case of failure or inaction on the part of the authorities in taking possession and paying the compensation to the landholders.

The mode of taking possession under the 1894 Act by drawing NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/12546/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/03/2026 undefined panchnama/inquest panchanma/memorandum has been held to be the approved mode of the transfer of possession.
With the drawing of panchnama, the land-in-question vested with the State Government.

There is no question of divesting after 1996 or after 2014, i.e. after commencement of 2013 Act, w.e.f.
1.1.2014.
15.

A bald assertion made in the writ petition that the petitioners and other villagers had refused to receive compensation and hence, it should be assumed that the compensation was not paid to the Amratlal Dharamchand Shah Since Decd.

4 petitioners is neither here nor there.

The Apex Court has clarified that, in case, a person has been tendered compensation, it is not open for him to claim that the acquisition lapsed under Section 24(2) due to non-payment or non-deposit of the compensation.

16. A careful reading of Section 24 of the 2013 Act indicates that it was a transitional provision and was applicable in cases where the land acquisition proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 though initiated but had not been concluded till the commencement of the 2013 Act, i.e. w.e.f.
01.01.2014.

However, in the present case, it is evident from the assertions made in the writ petition itself, that the land acquisition proceedings had been concluded logically with the making of the award and drawing of panchnama in the year 1996.

In accordance with Section 16 of the Act, 1894,
with the taking over of paper possession, the land-in- question vests absolutely in the State Government free from all encumbrances.

There is, thus, no question of applicability of Section 24(2)
of the 2013 Act in the facts and circumstances of the present case.

17. It is also observed by the Apex Court in Indore Development Authority (supra) that Section 24 does not provide NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/12546/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/03/2026 undefined an arm or tool to question the legality of the proceedings which have been undertaken under the 1894 Act and stood concluded before five years or more.

It was also noted therein that by and large, the concluded cases were questioned by way of invoking the provisions contained in Section 24 and it was held that the legality of concluded cases cannot be questioned under the guise of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act, as it does not envisage or confer such right to question the proceedings and the acquisitions having been concluded long back.

The challenge to the proceedings cannot be made within the parameters of Section 24(2) once panchnama had been drawn of taking possession, inasmuch as, the re-entry or retaining the possession is that of the trespassers.

The legality of proceedings cannot be challenged belatedly and the right to challenge cannot be revived by virtue of provisions of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act, as it only contemplates the lethargy/inaction of the authorities to act for five years or more.
It was observed that it is very easy to lay claim that physical possession was not taken with respect to the open land.

Yet, once vesting takes place, the possession is presumed to be that of the owner, i.e. the State Government, and the challenge under the purview of Section 24(2) cannot be entertained, as it is not what is remotely contemplated in Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.
18. In view of the above discussion, the prayers made in the present writ petition cannot be granted.

The writ petition is dismissed, following the decision of the Apex Court in Indore Development Authority (supra).
